title: Notification Center
summary: Open Notifications from the bell in the Agent header, Directory, or the Schedules navigation. /notifications brings together scheduled reminders, scheduled Agent outcomes, monitor alerts.
html:
Notification Center

Open Notifications from the bell in the Agent header, Directory, or the Schedules navigation. /notifications brings together scheduled reminders, scheduled Agent outcomes, monitor alerts, durable task updates and system notices.

Search matches title and message without regard to case. All includes unread, read and dismissed records; the other filters show each status separately. History starts with the newest 100 records. Load more expands it in steps of 100, up to the newest 500 retained records. Search and filters apply to the loaded set. The unread count covers all retained records, so it can exceed the number visible in this view.

Mark read, Mark all read and Dismiss are explicit actions. Dismiss retains the record in the Dismissed filter. Opening the Center normally, following a source link, displaying an alert or letting an alert disappear does not mark a notification read. Opening a specific /notifications?notification=ID link marks the item read if it was unread and focuses it when its card is visible. The saved status filter remains active; choose All and clear search if the selected item is hidden. Dismissed items remain dismissed.

View schedule opens Scheduler Manager. Open conversation is available when the existing public source context supplies a conversation ID. Notifications do not link to raw execution traces as their primary destination.

Messages display supported Markdown, including lists, emphasis, code, links and tables. Long messages start with a compact preview; Show more reveals the full message and Show less collapses it. Source links and notification actions stay in the card footer. Browser notifications and the small in-page alert use concise plain-text summaries; open the Center to read the formatted message.

Delivery while smTO is open

Use Enable browser notifications in the Center to request browser permission. smTO never requests it automatically on page load.

Browser state New notification delivery
Granted Native browser notification
Default / not enabled Compact in-page notification
Denied / blocked Compact in-page notification; no repeated permission prompt
Unsupported, or native construction fails Compact in-page notification

Browser permission and smTO's Notifications enabled preference in Mission Control are separate. The smTO preference is the master switch. Turning it off marks existing unread records read and stops native and in-page alerts; existing history remains visible. New arrivals are retained as read records with a suppression flag. Turning alerts back on does not restore their unread state or replay them as new alerts.

Native notifications also require a supported browser in a secure context. If the browser does not offer that capability, the in-page fallback still works while the page is active.

The in-page alert appears at the upper right on Agent, Schedules, Notifications and Mission Control. It displays one small icon, title and short message, and disappears after 6.5 seconds. Hovering or focusing it keeps it available. A burst shows up to three individual alerts sequentially, then one summary for the remainder. A hidden or unfocused tab waits to display pending alerts until it is active. Reduced-motion preferences disable the slide animation.

Clicking an in-page or native notification opens the specific item in Notification Center. A native click focuses its existing smTO window where the browser permits.

Initial history establishes a delivery baseline. Old unread records do not produce alerts on first load or reload. Recently delivered IDs and timestamps are remembered locally for up to seven days, capped at 500; notification content is never stored there. Tabs coordinate using recent IDs, browser messages and an optional short browser lock. Native notifications also use a stable ID tag. Browsers without these coordination features provide best-effort deduplication.

Native browser notifications require an active smTO page. This implementation does not add Web Push or background delivery after every smTO tab is closed. Missed alerts remain in durable Notification Center history, subject to existing retention.

Up next

The quiet right rail previews the next three direct reminders, ordered by the scheduler's saved next trigger. Eligible records have event_kind=scheduled, action_type=notification, status=active, and a valid next_run_at. Times use each reminder's configured timezone; hover for the full date, time and timezone. The rail moves below history on smaller screens.

Paused, cancelled, completed and unscheduled items are excluded. Conditional monitors and Agent schedules that notify upon completion are excluded because their notification time is not known in advance. Choose an item or View schedules to manage reminders in Scheduler Manager.

Notification changes and schedule changes refresh through the existing shared update stream. There is no additional polling channel, notification database or scheduler.

History, privacy and troubleshooting

Server retention is separate from the 500-item viewing limit. On insertion, the event store retains the newest max(100, AOR_AGENT_EVENTS_MAX_RUN_HISTORY) records; the setting defaults to 5000. Retention applies to unread, read and dismissed items alike. Dismissing an item keeps it in history until retention removes it; it does not cancel its source schedule, monitor or task.

The displayed copy uses the Notifications redaction preference and the public error-diagnostic boundary. These projections do not rewrite the stored message. Optional credential masking is not a guarantee that every message is safe to share; see Redaction. Notification delivery and inbox status are also separate from whether the source operation succeeded.

If an alert is missing, check the master preference, browser permission and whether an smTO page is open. For in-page alerts, activate and focus the tab. Initial history does not produce alerts, and another open tab may already have delivered the item. If history cannot refresh, use Retry after connectivity returns. A deep link outside the newest 500 retained items, or to an item removed by retention, reports that it is unavailable in recent history.

For the API, storage and update-stream owners, see Notification publication and observation.
